column4: description
Key, label or link that points to a record about the subject in this or another system.
Number assigned to the subject by a social security system.
Browser or client identification string sent by the subject's device.
Identifier of an authenticated or anonymous session of the subject; while the session is valid it grants access like a credential.
Team or working group the subject belongs to within the organization.
Department, service or other unit the subject belongs to.
Position or function the subject holds within the organization, such as head of unit or coordinator.
Start and end of the subject's assignment to a team, unit or role.
Nationality or citizenship of the subject.
Family or legal relationship between the subject and another person.
Philosophical or ethical convictions of the subject that are not religious, such as conscientious objection.
Membership of the subject in a trade union, including union dues deducted from pay.
Data concerning the sex life of the subject.
Data about the subject's studies and academic history, as a student or applicant.
Degree, program or qualification the subject is studying or has studied.
Registration of the subject in a program, course or academic period.
Courses the subject has taken, with their periods and outcomes.
Marks, grades or assessment results obtained by the subject.
Results of admission or standardized tests taken by the subject.
Studies completed by the subject before the current program.
Standing of the subject in a program: active, on leave, graduated, withdrawn.
Awards, honours, certificates and other merits of the subject.
Scholarships, grants and financial aid applied for or awarded to the subject.
Tuition, fees and charges owed or paid by the subject.
Type or degree of a disability of the subject.
Record of the actions the subject performed in a system: who did what and when.
Administrative infringements committed by the subject, the proceedings about them and the sanctions imposed, such as disciplinary or regulatory sanctions; criminal offences are user.criminal_history.
Recognition of the subject as a victim of gender-based violence, sexual violence, terrorism, trafficking or another offence, and the protection measures or entitlements it gives.
Secret, or a hash of a secret, that grants access: API keys, tokens, signing keys.
Access control definitions that do not identify a person: roles, permission matrices, scopes.
Evidence that protects the integrity of other data: hashes, chain anchors, checkpoints.
Settings and definitions that drive the system: menus, objects, parameters, rules.
Data about the organization and about third parties that are not natural persons.
Units, teams and their hierarchy.
Organizations and other legal persons: names, registration numbers, public registry data.
Sites, buildings, rooms and other places of the organization.
Definitions, documentation and management data of the organization's processes.
Business records that do not relate to a natural person.
Master data from public or standard sources.
Public code lists and registers: countries, currencies, languages, territorial codes, holidays.
